source_text: Quod ergo a veritate defunderis, quod fugaris, causae fecit deformitas quam tueris. Ceterum si ad Catholicos transire velles, quanto tute, id quod nos asserimus, elegantius exsequereris et plenius.
pass_a_gloss: That therefore you are poured out from the truth, that you are put to flight, the deformity of the cause which you protect has made. For the rest if you were willing to cross to the Catholics, how much more elegantly and more fully would you yourself carry out that which we assert.
pass_b_english: So the ugliness of the cause you defend has made truth rout you and drive you away. Otherwise, if you wished to come over to the catholics, how much more elegantly and fully you yourself would develop what I assert!

choices.why: Julian claims the catholic faith against Augustine; keep lowercase-c catholic as the universal church, not a later confessional brand.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
